correctness.rationale: A fully specified finite irreducible birth–death process has exact stationary detailed-balance ratios. All \(r_i\) relative to one are governed by \(G_i\); the discrete sign polynomial proves the unique minimum at \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1\). The modal-block classification explicitly includes equality shoulders/plateaus, and the vanishing-seed identity, discrete maximum and limit follow algebraically. The embedded exact rational checker independently evaluates detailed balance and stationarity and tests boundary values and all candidate threshold ties.

originality.rationale: The general stationary product formula is not claimed as original. The claim adds an exact discrete optimization over all local edge ratios, a unique critical edge index, tie-safe two-mode classification and an unexpected parity-paired nonmonotonic finite-size maximum; inspected literature instead addresses unseeded/deterministic bifurcations or a different q-SIS annihilation law. Targeted searches and accessible private prior-claim comparisons found no equivalent statement, but lack of a matching hit does not prove priority.

value.rationale: This resolves a motivated sharp finite-population stationary bimodality problem for triadic contagion with weak exogenous infection. The unique discrete edge index, tie-safe modal census, parity-paired asymptotic threshold and global maximum at population sizes 8–11 provide an informative finite-size boundary beyond a routine substitution into the generic stationary product formula.
